name: Reddish umber
lede: Reddish umber glosses Hatobanezumi, a Japanese traditional name that literally means dove feather grey, not umber.

sections.title: A gloss that drifts from its name
sections.body:
The library files this hex under *Hatobanezumi* (鳩羽鼠), whose kanji name a grey the color of a dove's feathers [1]. The English gloss "Reddish umber" describes the hue's warm, muted brown-grey rather than translating the Japanese name, so the two point at the same swatch by different routes [1]. [[umber]] is the English pigment word the gloss borrows, not a look-alike match; the hex #755D5B is a screen approximation, with no recipe or date recorded here [1].

Its nearest library look-alike is [[haematite-red]], about 4.6 units away in LCH space and read as darker and redder than this swatch [1].

Further along the same family are [[deep-livid-brown]] and [[faded-rosewood]], both read as more vivid than this swatch [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this hue appears in 316 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent, as photographed [2]. It is markedly more common after 1900, with Gustave Caillebotte, Mary Cassatt and Claude Monet among the painters it turns up most often in, relative to their total output [2]. These are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
